pass_a_gloss:
Their turning toward God. For walking in flesh we do not war according to flesh, for the weapons of our warfare are not fleshly but powerful through God. For those knowing to glory in wars and opposing those waging war against them fleshly would have fleshly armor and quite reasonably the full panoply, for helmet and breastplate weapons and swords and whatever they could conquer with; but for us the warfare and the manner of war requires spiritual weapons 358. And indeed the inspired Paul says that the soldier imagined in Christ must be adorned with these splendid armaments very well: for he puts on him a breastplate of righteousness and a helmet of salvation, and 'the sword of the Spirit which is the word of God,' and besides these still 'the shield of faith,' by which indeed all the fiery darts of the evil one are quenched. Therefore the weapons of the saints are not fleshly but rather spiritual and powerful through God, useful also for the overthrow of fortifications, I say of the Hellenic doctrines and heresies, and for exposing their reasonings as hostile, unskilled, and foolishly composed. Therefore let us overthrow such things and every height lifting itself up against the knowledge of God; we lead captive every thought to the obedience of Christ, instead of every height lifting itself up against God in thoughts of impiety we overthrow, and we glorify with the befitting voices, imagining nothing lowly about him.

For we will punish also others, bringing into a straight and utterly unerring path of thought, so that we may avenge every disobedience, when our obedience has been fulfilled; for it will be great in the kingdom of heaven not only the one who teaches, but also if anyone wishes to attach to the word the boastings from good works; since you are seeking proof, etc.; and indeed we are weak in him, but we will live with him by the power of God toward you; he threatens those in Corinth who have prematurely sinned, that if they do not wish to do what is fitting and to live holily, again he will not spare; and again the memory of the already aroused indignation he has; that indeed he will surely rebuke those who stumble, his word will be active, he tries to persuade further and as from those who have already passed by and those who are expected to come; in this connection he says, If you seek proof of Christ speaking in me; it is reasonable, he says, that you wait and also through the others to see whether at any time Christ speaks in me, and he brings to an end the modes of rebukes; do not think, he says, according to some of the unbelieving still and insolent that he is weak; for he is powerful in you, it is clear that to those who have believed and have been made by him, in whom also he grants the necessary concern, and he brings back those who err; therefore he is powerful in you; for he works as God and truly reveals the voices of the saints; and you will find my powerful word everywhere and always; for I am not the one speaking, myself, but Christ rather the one in me.

since moreover he makes mention of those who, from excessive simplicity, supposed that Christ truly was weak, on account of enduring the cross, and enduring the shamelessness, or impiety, of the Jews, he defends helpfully, bringing forth into the midst at the proper time the power of the mystery, and explaining the voluntary self-emptying of the Only-begotten, and the glory after this, its unsurpassable excellence. Yes, for he says, namely, that those who think they still have far to go in faith suppose that he was crucified from weakness, he suffered as a man, and he endured the death in flesh willingly, but it was necessary to know also that, having despoiled Hades and having bound the power of death, he rose again three days, not by human power using, but by divine and ineffable power.
pass_b_english: Their turning toward God. For though we walk in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh, since the weapons of our warfare are not fleshly but mighty through God to overthrow strongholds. Those who seek glory in battle and oppose their enemies in a carnal way would naturally possess carnal armor—helmet, breastplate, weapons, swords, and whatever tools they need to conquer—but our warfare demands spiritual weapons, as the inspired Paul declares.

He declares that the soldier imagined in Christ must be clothed in these splendid armaments: a breastplate of righteousness, a helmet of salvation, the sword of the Spirit which is the word of God, and the shield of faith, by which all the fiery darts of the evil one are extinguished. Therefore the weapons of the saints are not carnal but spiritual and powerful through God, effective for tearing down fortifications—not only of Hellenic doctrines and heresies but also for exposing their reasonings as hostile, unskilled, and foolishly woven.

Therefore let us tear down such strongholds and every proud idea that rises up against the knowledge of God. Let us take every thought captive to obey Christ, instead of overthrowing every idea that exalts itself against God in impious thoughts; let us praise Him with fitting voices, never imagining anything lowly about Him.

He helpfully brings up those who, from an excess of simplicity, imagined Christ to be truly weak, thinking that his endurance of the cross and his bearing of the Jews' shamelessness—or impiety—proved it. In defense, he places before us at the right moment the power of the mystery, explaining the voluntary self-emptying of the Only-begotten and the surpassing glory that followed.

Indeed, he says, those who imagine they still have far to go in faith suppose, according to their own view, that Christ was crucified from weakness, suffered as a man, and willingly endured the death of the flesh. But it is necessary to know this as well: having despoiled Hades and bound the power of death, he rose again on the third day—not by human strength, but by divine and ineffable power.

πολέμου τρόπος ὅπλων χρῄζει 358 πνευματικῶν. καὶ γοῦν ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος τὸν ἐν
Χριστῷ νοούμενον στρατιώτην, ταῖς οὕτω λαμπραῖς εὐοπλίαις κατασεμνύνεσθαι δεῖν εὖ
μάλα φησί· θώρακα μὲν γὰρ αὐτῷ περιτίθησι δικαιοσύνην, περικεφαλαίαν δὲ σωτηρίου,

τῆς πίστεως," δι' οὗ δὴ πάντα τὰ πεπυρωμένα τοῦ πονηροῦ κατασβέννυται βέλη. οὐκοῦν
οὐ σαρκικὰ τῶν ἁγίων τὰ βέλη, πνευματικὰ δὲ μᾶλλον καὶ δυνατὰ τῷ Θεῷ, χρήσιμά τε
πρὸς καθαίρεσιν ὀχυρωμάτων, τῶν ἑλληνικῶν δογμάτων φημὶ καὶ αἱρετικῶν, καὶ πρὸς
τὸ ἀποφαίνειν τοὺς ἐκείνων συλλογισμοὺς σαθρούς τε καὶ ἀτεχνεστάτους καὶ ἀσυνέτως

ὀνήσομεν γὰρ καὶ ἑτέρους, εἰς ὀρθὴν καὶ ἀπλανεστάτην ἐννοιῶν ἀποκομίζοντες τρίβον,
ὅπως ἐκδικήσωμεν πᾶσαν παρακοὴν, πληρωθείσης πρότερον τῆς ἡμῶν· ἔσται γὰρ μέγας
ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν οὐχ ὁ διδάξας μόνον, ἀλλ' εἴ τις τῷ λόγῳ προσεπάγειν
βούλοιτο τὰ ἐξ ἔργων ἀγαθῶν αὐχήματα.
Ἐπεὶ δοκιμὴν ζητεῖτε κ.τ.λ. Καὶ γὰρ ἡμεῖς ἀσθενοῦμεν ἐν αὐτῷ, ἀλλὰ ζησόμεθα
ἐν αὐτῷ ἐκ δυνάμεως Θεοῦ εἰς ὑμᾶς. Ἀπειλεῖ τοῖς ἐν Κορίνθῳ προημαρτηκόσιν, ὡς εἰ μὴ
βούλοιντο δρᾶν ἃ προσῆκε καὶ διαζῆν ἁγίως, πάλιν οὐ φείσεται· τὸ δέ Πάλιν τῆς ἤδη

παρῳχηκότων καὶ τῶν ἔσεσθαι προσδοκωμένων· ταύτῃτοί φησιν Εἰ δοκιμὴν ζητεῖτε τοῦ
ἐν ἐμοὶ λαλοῦντος Χριστοῦ. εἰκὸς γὰρ, φησὶ, περιμένετε καὶ διὰ τῶν δευτέρων ἰδεῖν

ἰσχύοντα πάντη τε καὶ πάντως εὑρήσετε λόγον· εἰμὶ γὰρ ὁ λαλῶν οὐκ αὐτὸς ἐγὼ,

οἰηθέντων ἀληθῶς ἀσθενῆσαι Χριστὸν, διά τοι τὸ ὑπομεῖναι σταυρὸν, καὶ τῆς Ἰουδαίων
